Chapter 6: Responding to Challenges Without Fear
You know that feeling when someone puts your beliefs on the spot? Maybe it’s in a classroom, maybe around the dinner table, or maybe it’s just those nagging questions in your own mind. Suddenly, the questions start flying— “How can you believe in miracles?” or “What about all the suffering in the world?” Sometimes even, “Isn’t faith just wishful thinking?” It can feel like you’re on trial, and the pressure to have the perfect answer is real.
But here’s the thing—no one has all the answers. Not even the wisest thinkers out there. What really sets confident people apart isn’t being able to win every debate. It’s about showing up with honesty, listening carefully, and responding with both humility and courage.
Let me share a story. There’s a nurse I know, and one day she found herself in a break room conversation about prayer. Out of nowhere, a coworker scoffed and said, “If God really cared, why do bad things keep happening?” You can imagine the knot in her stomach. She wanted to speak up for her faith, but she didn’t want to sound flippant or dismissive either. So, she paused, took a deep breath, and said, “I don’t have all the answers. But I do believe that God is with us, even in the hardest moments.”
The conversation didn’t end then and there, but something changed. Instead of a heated argument, it turned into a real exchange—one where both people actually listened to each other.
Most folks don’t realize it’s totally okay not to have a perfect response every time. What matters more is your attitude—being open, respectful, and quietly confident that your faith can handle tough questions. Sometimes, the best thing you can do is ask a thoughtful question back, or share a story about how your faith has shaped your life.
That nurse discovered something important: faith isn’t about winning arguments. It’s about living with integrity. And the more she practiced this, the less afraid she was of those tough conversations. She saw it’s possible to stand firm without getting defensive, to be honest about doubts without losing hope.
In a world that often mixes up confidence with certainty, it’s easy to forget that real strength actually comes from facing tough stuff head-on. The journey of faith isn’t about having everything figured out—it’s about believing that searching for the truth is worth it.
